sections.content: How many people are "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers"?

23,170 people

were counted on the census as "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Launderers, dry cleaners and pressers undertake the washing, dry cleaning, ironing and pressing of clothing, household and other linen, carpets, curtains and other articles.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers", 16.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" included:

  • market and street traders and assistants
  • housekeepers and related occupations
  • upholsterers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" there were more women than men (67.5% compared with 32.5%).

This means "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "elementary administration and service occupations".

Men made up 32.5% and women made up 67.5% of "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" included:

  • teachers of english as a foreign language
  • public services associate professionals
  • events managers and organisers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "launderers, dry cleaners and pressers", 12.7% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work part-time than full-time (57% compared with 43%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (81.5%) than self-employed (18.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
